title: Appealing a Decline Due to UIF Registration
description: What to do if SASSA declines your grant claiming you are receiving UIF when you are not. Step-by-step guide to getting a UI-19 form and submitting your appeal.

seo.metaTitle: Appealing SASSA Decline Due to UIF Registration — Complete Guide
seo.metaDescription: Guide to appealing a SASSA grant decline caused by UIF registration. Learn how to get a UI-19 termination letter from the Department of Labour and submit it with your ITSAA appeal.

contentBlocks.text: Appealing a Decline Due to UIF Registration

A very common reason for grant rejection is 'UIF Registered'. This happens because SASSA's database checks find your ID registered on the Department of Labour's UIF database, even if you are no longer receiving payments.
This guide is for SASSA applicants who received a decline status because their ID number is linked to a UIF record, even if they are no longer receiving UIF payments.

steps.title: Visit the Department of Labour
steps.description: Visit your local Department of Labour office to request a UI-19 form or a UIF Status Letter.

steps.title: Get proof of termination
steps.description: Ensure the letter clearly states your employment has terminated and you are no longer receiving monthly UIF payouts.

steps.title: Make a copy
steps.description: Scan or take a clear photo of this official letter.

steps.title: Submit your appeal
steps.description: Submit your appeal online via the ITSAA portal and upload the proof of UIF termination, or present it at a SASSA office.

contentBlocks.title: Timeline
contentBlocks.text: Submit as soon as you receive the decline, within 90 days. The Department of Labour can take 5-10 days to print your status letter.

items: UI-19 form or official UIF status confirmation letter
Employer failed to update your termination status with the Department of Labour
Legacy database error on the state servers

faqs.question: Why did SASSA say I have UIF when I was retrenched years ago?
faqs.answer: This is almost always because your former employer never submitted your UI-19 termination form to the Department of Labour, leaving your status active on their database.
